outputs.L3:
The method automatically produces and finishes toothings on workpieces using two workpiece spindles, a hobbing tool, and a deburring device. First, an unmachined workpiece is loaded onto the first workpiece spindle at a first loading position. The spindle transports the workpiece to the hobbing tool, where a milling operation is performed to produce the desired toothing.

After milling, the first spindle returns the machined workpiece to the first loading position and receives another unmachined workpiece. The milled workpiece is then transferred through an intermediate storage area to a second loading position, where it is received by the second workpiece spindle.

The second spindle transports the milled workpiece to the deburring device, which removes burrs created during the milling operation. This deburring process is carried out concurrently with the milling of another workpiece by the first spindle. By overlapping the milling and deburring operations, the method enables continuous, automated production while reducing overall processing and idle times.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to an automated method and apparatus for machining toothed workpieces, particularly for carrying out hobbing and subsequent deburring operations in a coordinated production sequence. The apparatus includes first and second workpiece spindles, each configured to receive and rotationally drive a workpiece. The workpiece spindles are assigned separate loading positions and can transport the workpieces between the loading positions and respective machining stations. A hobbing tool is provided for generating or finishing the teeth of a workpiece, while a separate deburring device removes burrs produced during the hobbing operation.

In operation, an unmachined workpiece is loaded onto the first workpiece spindle at a first loading position and is then transferred to the hobbing station. The workpiece is rotated and machined in engagement with the hobbing tool to produce the desired tooth geometry. After hobbing has been completed, the workpiece is removed from the hobbing station and placed in an intermediate storage location. The intermediate storage decouples the hobbing operation from the downstream deburring operation and temporarily holds one or more hobbed workpieces until the deburring device is available.

A hobbed workpiece is subsequently removed from the intermediate storage and loaded onto the second workpiece spindle, preferably at a second loading position. The second spindle transports the workpiece to the deburring device, where burrs and sharp edges resulting from the hobbing process are removed. Once deburring is complete, the finished workpiece is returned to the second loading position and unloaded for further processing, inspection, or collection.

The movements and operating cycles of the two workpiece spindles are coordinated so that the hobbing and deburring stages can be performed at least partly simultaneously. Thus, while a first workpiece is being hobbed on the first spindle, a previously hobbed workpiece can be deburred on the second spindle. At the same time, loading and unloading operations may be carried out at the respective loading positions whenever the associated spindle is available. The intermediate storage compensates for differences in the cycle times of the two machining stages and reduces the need for either station to remain idle.

By separating the loading and handling paths for the hobbing and deburring operations, the method permits efficient parallel processing without requiring a single workpiece spindle to perform every transport and machining step. The arrangement can therefore shorten overall cycle times, improve utilization of the hobbing tool and deburring device, and increase production throughput. Automated controls may synchronize the spindles, tools, storage system, and loading devices, enabling continuous and reliable manufacture of deburred toothed workpieces.

### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language. Although it is short and simple, it plays an essential role in communication. Known as the definite article, “the” is used before a noun when referring to a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “the book” points to a particular book rather than any book.

The word also helps create shared understanding. When someone says, “Close the door,” both speaker and listener usually know which door is meant. In this way, “the” provides clarity and context.

Despite its modest appearance, “the” demonstrates how even the smallest words can carry significant meaning. Without it, English would often sound less natural and precise.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a method for milling toothings onto workpieces and subsequently deburring them, using separate loading positions and spindles. Include temporary storage between stations and specify that one workpiece can be deburred while another is being hobbed.
counterfactuals.output:
A method for machining workpieces comprises:

1. Loading a first workpiece at a first loading position onto a hobbing spindle.
2. Milling a toothing onto the first workpiece by hobbing.
3. Transferring the hobbed first workpiece to a temporary storage position.
4. Removing the first workpiece from the temporary storage position and loading it at a second, separate loading position onto a deburring spindle.
5. Deburring the toothing on the deburring spindle.
6. Unloading the deburred workpiece.

The hobbing spindle and deburring spindle are operated independently, such that the first workpiece is deburred while a second workpiece, loaded at the first loading position, is simultaneously being hobbed. Temporary storage buffers the workpieces between the hobbing and deburring stations.

### What is claimed is:

1. **An automated machine tool for machining workpieces, comprising:**  
   a machine frame;  
   a first workpiece spindle (3) configured to releasably hold and rotationally drive a first workpiece;  
   a second workpiece spindle (3′) configured to releasably hold and rotationally drive a second workpiece;  
   a hobbing tool (12) configured to perform a hobbing operation on a workpiece held by either of the first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′);  
   a deburring device (10) configured to deburr a workpiece held by either of the first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′);  
   first and second loading positions (19, 19′) respectively accessible by the first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′);  
   an intermediate storage unit (14) configured to temporarily receive at least one workpiece; and  
   a controller configured to control movement and operation of the first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′) such that a workpiece is transferable among at least one of the loading positions (19, 19′), the hobbing tool (12), the deburring device (10), and the intermediate storage unit (14).

2. The automated machine tool of claim 1, wherein the first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′) are movable independently of one another.

3. The automated machine tool of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to cause the hobbing tool (12) to machine a workpiece held by one of the first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′) while another workpiece held by the other of the first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′) is loaded, unloaded, deburred, or transferred to or from the intermediate storage unit (14).

4. The automated machine tool of claim 1, wherein the intermediate storage unit (14) is positioned within a working region accessible by both the first workpiece spindle (3) and the second workpiece spindle (3′).

5. The automated machine tool of claim 1, wherein the intermediate storage unit (14) comprises at least one workpiece receptacle configured to retain a partially machined workpiece between the hobbing operation and a deburring operation.

6. The automated machine tool of claim 1, wherein the first loading position (19) is assigned to the first workpiece spindle (3), and the second loading position (19′) is assigned to the second workpiece spindle (3′).

7. The automated machine tool of claim 1, wherein each of the first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′) is configured to receive an unmachined workpiece at a respective one of the loading positions (19, 19′) and to discharge a machined workpiece at the respective loading position.

8. The automated machine tool of claim 1, wherein the hobbing tool (12) is arranged at a machining station and is configured to generate teeth on a circumferential surface of a workpiece.

9. The automated machine tool of claim 8, wherein the deburring device (10) is arranged at a deburring station spaced from the machining station.

10. The automated machine tool of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to execute a workpiece-exchange sequence comprising:  
   placing, by the first workpiece spindle (3), a first workpiece in the intermediate storage unit (14);  
   removing, by the second workpiece spindle (3′), the first workpiece from the intermediate storage unit (14); and  
   presenting, by the second workpiece spindle (3′), the first workpiece to the hobbing tool (12) or the deburring device (10).

11. The automated machine tool of claim 1, wherein the intermediate storage unit (14) provides a buffer permitting operation of the hobbing tool (12) to continue independently of a loading or unloading operation at one of the loading positions (19, 19′).

12. The automated machine tool of claim 1, further comprising a loading apparatus configured to supply unmachined workpieces to, and remove machined workpieces from, the first and second loading positions (19, 19′).

13. The automated machine tool of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to coordinate rotation of a workpiece spindle with rotation or translation of the hobbing tool (12) during the hobbing operation.

14. The automated machine tool of claim 1, wherein the deburring device (10) is configured to remove burrs from at least one axial end of teeth formed in a workpiece by the hobbing tool (12).

15. **A method of operating an automated machine tool having first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′), a hobbing tool (12), a deburring device (10), first and second loading positions (19, 19′), and an intermediate storage unit (14), the method comprising:**  
   receiving a first workpiece with the first workpiece spindle (3) at the first loading position (19);  
   receiving a second workpiece with the second workpiece spindle (3′) at the second loading position (19′);  
   machining at least one of the first and second workpieces with the hobbing tool (12);  
   deburring at least one of the first and second workpieces with the deburring device (10);  
   temporarily storing at least one of the first and second workpieces in the intermediate storage unit (14); and  
   independently controlling the first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′) to transfer the first and second workpieces among the loading positions (19, 19′), the hobbing tool (12), the deburring device (10), and the intermediate storage unit (14).

16. The method of claim 15, further comprising machining a workpiece held by the first workpiece spindle (3) with the hobbing tool (12) concurrently with loading, unloading, deburring, or intermediately storing a workpiece handled by the second workpiece spindle (3′).

17. The method of claim 15, further comprising transferring a partially machined workpiece from one of the first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′) to the intermediate storage unit (14), and subsequently retrieving the partially machined workpiece from the intermediate storage unit (14) with the other of the first and second workpiece spindles (3, 3′).

18. The method of claim 15, wherein machining with the hobbing tool (12) comprises forming circumferential teeth on a workpiece, and wherein deburring comprises removing burrs formed adjacent at least one axial end of the circumferential teeth.

19. The method of claim 15, further comprising selecting, by a controller, a transfer sequence based on an availability state of at least one of the hobbing tool (12), the deburring device (10), the loading positions (19, 19′), and the intermediate storage unit (14).

20. The method of claim 15, further comprising using the intermediate storage unit (14) as a workpiece buffer to reduce idle time of the hobbing tool (12).
